metadata.bookend_exempt_reason: Rithika's script is eight beats, read verbatim, with a hard 4:00 maximum. (1) Runtime: the hesitant writer, key-terms card and Your Turn composer would add narration outside her script and push past 4:00. (2) Branding: those components carry the instructor's identity, which this student film may not show. (3) Beat 1 already introduces the persona and the problem; beat 3 defines the terms (gates, HELD, CLOSED, OVER-LEVEL). The outro is never exempt: beat 8 is BOUT, drawn in Manim with the film title.

beats.script_text: Hi, I'm Rithika. This is my mode for the Reallocation Engine. It's built for Sasha Jones, a fictional F-1 master's student in data science. She graduates in December 2026, her OPT work permit should start in January 2027, and she's applying for entry-level Data Scientist roles that sponsor an H-1B. Like most students, she finds them on aggregator sites.

beats.script_text: Here's what Sasha can't see. A job page can look open long after the employer closed the role. She can't tell whether a company that sponsors visas sponsors this role, or whether a live posting is even her level. And every dead application costs time, because once OPT starts she gets only ninety days of unemployment.

beats.script_text: The mode runs gates in order. G1 checks the company in the engine's sponsorship data. G2 checks the job is live, and an aggregator saying "active" is never enough on its own. A level check makes sure the title fits an entry-level candidate. G3 checks the visa timeline, and G4 is a human. These are gates, not votes. A role that fails one never gets a score: it's held, closed, or over-level.

beats.script_text: Then I opened the pages myself, as the G4 human, and found two bugs in the existing checker. An Airbnb link scored Apply, but it redirected through Greenhouse's own error page to a general job list. And on a Nextdoor page, the checker missed an Apply button I could see.

beats.script_text: So I fixed both inside my mode. Run 2 asks Greenhouse's job API for the actual job record, follows every redirect, and only trusts known employer and hiring-system sites. Airbnb became Closed, and Nextdoor became live. But that exposed a new problem: two Senior jobs now scored Apply for an entry-level student. Run 3 added a level gate on the title. Against my own decisions on the five postings I reviewed, agreement went three of five, then two, then four.

beats.script_text: Two honest caveats. Those rules were checked on the same five postings I reviewed, so that isn't a held-out test. And some things it still can't see. Figma's title just says "Data Scientist," but the description asks for experience. Sponsorship data is company-wide. And only Greenhouse has a record check so far.
